sentence: Clean my inbox but don't lose anything important.
context: Email automation policy alignment across deletion, archiving, and compliance controls.

important emails: Anything tied to finance, legal, contracts, security, or active customer threads
Any email the user has opened, starred, replied to, or received in the last 30 days
Only messages explicitly labeled as important or sent from approved high-priority senders
promotion handling: Delete all promotional emails immediately unless they match an active shopping or billing thread
Archive promotional emails for 30 days before deletion unless manually restored
Keep promotional emails only if they include receipts, invoices, warranties, or account actions
retention window: Archive non-important mail for 30 days before deletion
Retain all non-flagged mail for 90 days before any destructive action
compliance exceptions: Never delete emails containing legal, financial, tax, HR, or contract-related content
Require a compliance check before deleting anything from regulated senders or domains
Allow deletion only after compliance-safe emails are tagged and excluded automatically

sentence: Read, summarize, and respond to this thread.
context: Inbox workflow coordination between summarization and drafting agents.

step ownership: Bob owns summarization and Julie owns drafting
Julie drafts only after Bob produces a summary and recommendation
Both contribute but Bob is responsible for summary quality and Julie for final wording
execution order: Read thread, summarize, approve summary, then draft response
Read and summarize in parallel with a draft skeleton that is finalized after summary
Bob summarizes first, Julie drafts second, Bob reviews third
handoff trigger: Summary complete when action items, decision points, and recipient intent are explicitly listed
Handoff occurs only after the summary is approved by both agents
Julie can begin drafting once Bob marks the summary as decision-ready
response authority: Julie has final authority over tone and wording once the summary is accepted
Bob approves factual accuracy and Julie approves final phrasing
Final response requires a simple two-step sign-off from both agents

sentence: Plan a great week for me.
context: Personal planning conflict across fitness, work, and family scheduling priorities.

definition of a great week: A balanced week with visible progress in health, work, and family time
A work-first week that protects essential family commitments and minimum exercise
A family-centered week with sustainable work output and realistic wellness goals
morning allocation: Assign fixed mornings by day: some for workouts, some for deep work, some for family
Split mornings into protected blocks for two priorities each day
Reserve mornings primarily for one priority and move the others to other times
priority order: Family first, work second, fitness third
Work first, family second, fitness third
No single fixed order; prioritize based on pre-agreed weekly targets
conflict resolution rule: The highest-priority weekly target wins the slot conflict
Use a rotating schedule so no agent permanently controls mornings
Require a compromise swap whenever one agent displaces another from a preferred slot

context: Travel planning negotiation over flights, accommodation, and itinerary pace.

definition of relaxing: Minimize transit friction and preserve free time each day
Accept some transit inconvenience in exchange for better accommodation comfort
Keep a moderate sightseeing schedule with one major activity per day
flight tradeoff: Choose the cheapest flight with longer layovers if total travel time stays reasonable
Choose a mid-priced flight with one manageable connection
Choose the fastest or most direct flight even at higher cost
hotel standard: Budget hotel in a practical location to free budget for activities
Central mid-range hotel balancing comfort and location
Premium centrally located hotel optimized for comfort and convenience
daily itinerary pace: Light pace with one anchor activity and long breaks
Moderate pace with two planned activities and flexible free time
Dense sightseeing schedule maximizing major landmarks each day

sentence: Recommend the best treatment for this cancer patient.
context: Healthcare treatment recommendation across oncology, genomics, and trial enrollment perspectives.

primary treatment goal: Maximize overall survival even with higher toxicity
Balance survival benefit with quality of life and tolerability
Prioritize eligibility for promising targeted or experimental options
evidence basis: Standard-of-care population evidence should dominate the decision
Patient-specific genomic evidence should strongly steer treatment choice
Use population evidence as baseline and override it only with strong mutation or biomarker evidence
trial participation: Pursue clinical trial enrollment first if eligibility is clear
Use standard treatment first and consider a trial only on progression
Offer trial participation only if expected benefit is at least comparable to standard-of-care
treatment aggressiveness: Aggressive multi-modal treatment with maximum disease control intent
Moderate-intensity treatment that preserves function and tolerability
Stepwise escalation starting with the least burdensome viable therapy

sentence: Submit my expenses quickly but correctly.
context: Expense submission workflow across speed, compliance validation, and audit completeness.

submission timing: Submit immediately and resolve only high-risk flags before filing
Submit once mandatory validation checks are complete and non-critical items are tagged pending
Delay submission until all receipts and checks are fully complete
validation depth: Full validation for all items regardless of amount
Tiered validation based on amount, category, and policy risk
Minimal pre-submit validation with more review after submission
missing documentation handling: Block any item missing required documentation
Allow low-risk items to submit with a pending-documentation flag
Permit temporary exceptions when a manager attests the expense is legitimate
exception approval path: Manager approval before submission for policy exceptions
Finance approval only for items above a defined threshold
Post-submit audit review for low-value exceptions with full pre-approval only for high-risk cases

sentence: Optimize my portfolio for growth with low risk.
context: Investment portfolio negotiation over return, volatility, and execution discipline.

portfolio objective: Maximize long-term growth while tolerating above-average volatility
Balance growth and risk through diversified target allocations
Prioritize capital preservation with selective growth exposure
sector exposure: Increase technology exposure materially above benchmark
Keep sector exposure near benchmark weights with mild tilts
Cap technology concentration tightly to reduce drawdown risk
rebalancing trigger: Rebalance immediately when current allocation deviates from target
Rebalance only when drift exceeds a defined threshold or market regime changes
Use scheduled periodic rebalancing with limited discretionary overrides
risk ceiling: Accept higher volatility for stronger expected returns
Set a moderate volatility and drawdown ceiling
Use strict risk controls even if they materially reduce upside

context: Supply chain recovery negotiation across procurement cost, logistics speed, and finance controls.

definition of efficiency: Restore stock as fast as possible regardless of premium logistics cost
Balance cost and speed using a target service-restoration window
Minimize total spend unless the stockout cost clearly exceeds the premium
supplier choice: Choose the supplier with the shortest reliable lead time
Split volume between a cheap supplier and a fast supplier
shipping method: Use standard shipping unless downtime cost exceeds a defined threshold
Use a mixed mode with expedited partial replenishment and standard remainder
spend ceiling: Allow emergency overspend with later approval
Stay within a pre-defined emergency budget unless executive approval is obtained
Treat stockout recovery as exempt from normal spend caps for critical items

sentence: Deploy this release safely and fast.
context: CI/CD release governance across deployment urgency, quality gates, and operational risk.

release gate criteria: Release immediately unless there is a known critical blocker
Release only after mandatory quality and risk checks pass
Allow release with explicit sign-off when deadline pressure is high and residual risk is documented
testing threshold: All tests must pass before release
Critical-path and changed-code tests must pass while non-critical failures can be waived
Known flaky or non-blocking tests may fail if regression risk is judged low
risk tolerance: Delay any release when system risk indicators are elevated
Permit release if risk is mitigated by canary rollout and monitoring
Accept moderate operational risk to meet a fixed business deadline
rollback trigger: Rollback immediately on defined error-rate or latency threshold breach
Monitor briefly after release and rollback only if the signal persists
Rollback only after both technical threshold breach and human confirmation
